plan.title: policy-changes.log holds two contradictory no-op conventions; 63 of 236 rows record nothing (#1250 vs typed-policy writers)

narratives.Description: Typed-policy writers append meta/policy-changes.log even on no-op while the #1250 welcome path suppresses those rows. That contradiction dirties the tree during task check and dilutes a security ledger. Pick one convention, record it, and stop no-op appends from leaving a tracked dirty file.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

`meta/policy-changes.log` carries two contradictory no-op conventions. The typed-policy verbs append an audit row even when nothing changed; the #1250 welcome path suppresses it. Neither is recorded as a decision. The "always append" side dominates, and 63 of the ledger's 236 rows now record that nothing happened.

The operational cost is that a read-only-in-effect verb dirties a tracked file, which trips release Step 1 pre-flight.

## Observed

During the v0.105.0 cut, `task check` ran a `product-signal:enable` and left the tree dirty with:

```
2026-08-20T00:28:20Z actor=task product-signal:enable productSignal.enabled=true
  sinkRepo=deftai/product-signal previous={"enabled":true,"sinkRepo":"deftai/product-signal"}
```

New value equals previous value.

Ledger composition (236 rows):

| Rows | Verb | Real transitions |
|---|---|---|
| 64 | `product-signal:enable` | **1** (the initial `previous=null` on 2026-07-23) |
| 45 | `policy:enforce-branches` | 45 — genuine |
| 45 | `policy:allow-direct-commits` | 45 — genuine |
| 82 | assorted `actor=deft` one-offs | genuine |

The 90 enforce/allow rows are repetitive but legitimate — they are the release ritual flipping branch protection off and back on, and each is a real state change. The no-op population is the 63 `product-signal:enable` rows.

## This is deliberate, which is the actual problem

`packages/core/src/policy/product-signal.ts:256-276` computes `changedFlag`, guards the PROJECT-DEFINITION write on it, then appends unconditionally:

```ts
const changedFlag =
  previousNormalized.enabled !== nextBlock.enabled ||
  previousNormalized.sinkRepo !== nextBlock.sinkRepo;
policyBlock.productSignal = nextBlock;
if (changedFlag) {
  atomicWriteProjectDefinition(path, data);   // write is guarded
}
...
appendAuditLog(projectRoot, parts.join(" "));  // append is not
```

and says so to the operator:

```
no-op: value already matched (audit entry still appended for trail).
```

The same shape and the same string appear in `ceremony-dial.ts:756`, `value-feedback.ts:405`, and `require-human-merge.ts:422`. So the typed-policy family consistently chose "record the attempt."

#1250 chose the opposite for the wipCap welcome path (`packages/core/src/triage/welcome/onboard.ts:115`), where accepting the default deliberately does **not** materialize the field or write a row.

Both positions are defensible. Recording attempts has real value for a security-relevant ledger — "who tried to flip this and when" is not nothing. Suppressing no-ops keeps the trail readable. What is not defensible is holding both in the same file with no decision explaining which applies where.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

1. **Tree dirtying before a release.** The append happens during `task check`, so a verb that changed no state leaves a tracked file modified. Release Step 1 is `git status --porcelain`, so this must be reverted or committed before every cut. It surfaced exactly that way on v0.105.0.
2. **Signal dilution in a security artifact.** This ledger is the audit trail for `allowDirectCommitsToMaster` transitions (#746/#747) and was hardened against symlink redirection in #2470. It is meant to be read during incident review. A quarter of it saying "nothing changed" is the failure mode audit logs die of.
3. **The `previous=` field already carries the information.** A reader can distinguish a real transition from a no-op by comparing new against `previous` — but only by parsing every row, which is what suppression or an explicit token would avoid.

## Proposed change

Pick one convention and record it. Either direction closes this:

**Option A — suppress no-ops.** Guard `appendAuditLog` on `changedFlag` in the four typed-policy writers, matching #1250. Simplest, and makes the ledger all-signal.

**Option B — keep recording attempts, mark them.** Add an explicit `changed=true|false` token to the row and keep appending. `content/UPGRADING.md:868` documents exactly this token for the `actor=triage-welcome` rows, so the format precedent already exists in-tree. A reader greps `changed=true` for the transition history. This preserves the "who tried" value that the current copy is reaching for.

**Either way**, the no-op append must stop dirtying the tree during `task check`, or `product-signal:enable` should not run there at all.

Option B is the better fit if the "for trail" intent is genuine, because it keeps the evidence and makes it filterable. Option A is right if that intent was never load-bearing.

⊗ Rewriting or pruning existing rows. The ledger is append-only by design (#746) and hardened (#2470); historical no-op rows stay.

## Acceptance

- One convention applies to every writer of `meta/policy-changes.log`, recorded as a decision (`task decision:write`) naming which and why.
- `#1250`'s welcome path and the typed-policy verbs agree.
- A `product-signal:enable` that changes nothing does not leave a tracked file modified after `task check`.
- If Option B: rows carry a machine-readable changed token, and `content/UPGRADING.md:868`'s existing `changed=` documentation is generalized to cover them.
- Existing rows are untouched.

## Affected writers

- `packages/core/src/policy/product-signal.ts:275`
- `packages/core/src/policy/ceremony-dial.ts:756`
- `packages/core/src/policy/value-feedback.ts:405`
- `packages/core/src/policy/require-human-merge.ts:422`
- `packages/core/src/policy/org-force-on-migration.ts:565`
- shared sink: `packages/core/src/policy/resolve.ts:208` (`appendAuditLog`)

Refs #746, #747, #1250, #1186, #2470, #2980
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer, I want one recorded no-op convention for policy-changes.log, so that task check cannot dirty a security ledger when nothing changed.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Guard appendAuditLog in packages/core/src/policy/product-signal.ts and sibling writers on changedFlag or stamp changed=true|false, matching the #1250 welcome module.
2. Add tests that assert a no-op product-signal:enable leaves meta/policy-changes.log unmodified and existing rows stay intact.
narratives.Decisions: - xbrief/decisions/2026-08-20-policy-changes-log-records-real-transitions-only-written-rows-st.decision.json — Policy-changes.log records real transitions only. Written rows stamp changed=true. No-op verbs do not append.

narrative.Acceptance: When the story lands, task decision:write records which no-op convention applies to every writer of meta/policy-changes.log and why.
When a typed-policy verb and the #1250 welcome path run, both follow the same recorded convention instead of contradictory append versus suppress behavior.

items.title: No-op enable does not dirty the tree

narrative.Acceptance: When product-signal:enable matches the current value during task check, git status returns a clean tree for meta/policy-changes.log.
When the convention ships, existing ledger rows remain byte-identical and are not rewritten or pruned.
